title: Tanzanian Banana Fritters
community: The evening street dessert — sweet banana fritters
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Ndizi za Kukaanga — ripe bananas dipped in a light, slightly sweetened batter and deep-fried until golden and crispy outside, melting and sweet within. The evening street dessert fritter — warm, golden, and irresistible.
longDesc: Banana fritters are the sweet street food of Tanzanian evenings — the ripe bananas coated in a simple batter and fried until the outside is golden and crispy while the banana inside caramelises in its own sweetness. Simple, affordable, and completely satisfying.
ingredients: Honey or powdered sugar to serve
steps: Make batter: whisk flour, sugar, cardamom, salt and water until smooth.
Dip banana halves in batter — coat completely.
Fry 3—4 minutes until golden on all sides.
Drizzle with honey or dust with powdered sugar.
chefTips: Very ripe bananas — sweeter, more flavourful.
The batter should be smooth but not too thick.
Serve immediately — they lose crispiness as they cool.
cookingScience: See TZA129 for fritter frying science.
sustainabilityTips: Over-ripe bananas that would otherwise go to waste — perfect for fritters.
culturalNote: Banana fritters are the sweet ending to a Tanzanian evening — bought from a vendor as the night market winds down, eaten warm from the paper bag, the cardamom and caramelised banana the last taste of the day.
